title: 1Password confirms hackers stole customer data, but not their passwords
summary: Watch out for unexpected recovery emails and invitations.
content: TL;DR 1Password has confirmed a security breach that exposed some customers’ personal information, including names and email addresses. The company says no customer passwords were exposed and that users don’t need to change their account or saved passwords. 1Password recommends watching out for unexpected account recovery emails and invitations following the breach. Trust is everything when you’re in the business of keeping people’s passwords safe. It’s a responsibility that has only grown for 1Password in recent months, with the company enabling Claude and, more recently, other AI agents to sign into websites without exposing users’ credentials. That trust is now being put to the test after 1Password confirmed a security breach that exposed some customer information, although it maintains that users’ passwords are safe. In a blog post published on November 25, 1Password revealed that it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting suspicious activity involving an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker gained access to the company’s source code and compromised backend services, obtaining customer names, email addresses, account identifiers, and other account information.

title: Android 17 is getting a new setting to prevent unwanted Bluetooth audio switching
summary: Google looks set to borrow a handy feature from Apple's iOS 26 playbook.
content: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google is working on a new Android 17 feature that lets users keep audio playing through their headphones even when another device connects. The feature, called Keep audio in headphones, should appear in Connection preferences once it goes live. It’s similar to Apple’s Keep Audio with Headphones feature from iOS 26, which prevents audio from switching to a car or other connected device. Google could soon make one small but useful change to how Android handles Bluetooth audio . We’ve spotted a new feature in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 that could let users keep audio playing through their headphones even when another audio device, such as a car stereo or Bluetooth speaker, connects to their phone. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We spotted the feature, called “Keep audio in headphones,” in the latest Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 build. The setting comes with a straightforward description: “Always play audio in your headphones when other audio devices like speakers and cars connect to this device.”

title: Android Auto is working on a new Details page for easier bug reporting

We also found a relocated speedometer in Google Maps, plus a bunch of new manufacturer icons that could land in a future update. Android Auto is no stranger to bugs , and a future version of the app could make it easier to submit your device/car information in bug reports. Google is working on an updated Connected vehicles page with a new option to instantly copy and share relevant details. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We examined Android Auto version 18.3.164844 to enable a new Details option from the Android Auto settings page. This opens a “Vehicle information” dialog containing all the necessary information, including the car’s make and model, software version, display dimensions, and more.

title: Google is working on gamepad profiles for Android’s controller remapping feature
summary: You might not have to remap your controller every time you launch a different game.
content: TL;DR Google is working on adding support for multiple gamepad profiles in Android. Code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 hints at a new interface for managing gamepad profiles. The feature could let users switch between gamepad button layouts on the fly. If you’re a mobile gamer, you probably use controllers for many Android games . Customizing a controller’s layout can be quite useful, especially if you like using different layouts for different games. Although Google added support for game controller remapping with Android 17 , it currently lets you keep only one layout saved at a time. Fortunately, Google is now working to improve the feature with support for multiple gamepad profiles. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. While digging through the code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 , we spotted several strings that point to an upcoming gamepad profile management interface. According to the strings, there could be a “Default” profile, along with options to edit and delete individual profiles. We also spotted strings hinting at a “More options” menu for each profile.

title: These are the best times to buy a new phone if you want to save money
summary: Don’t pay full price for your next flagship. Here’s when Samsung, Google and Apple phones get their biggest discounts.
content: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority Buying a flagship phone on launch day without a good trade-in deal is one of the easiest ways to overspend in 2026. Smartphone prices are shooting northwards, largely because of growing demand for AI components in data centers and constrained supply for practically everything else, including smartphones. You’d be surprised to learn that memory costs have gone from accounting for 13% of a phone’s total component costs in early 2025 to more than 40% by late 2026. As a result, major brands have passed those costs on to buyers. Flagships like the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro now start $100 higher than their predecessors and spending well over $1,000 on a new phone is becoming the norm.

title: The Blurams F20C solar camera sees what my video doorbell misses
summary: This outdoor security camera was able to solve my problem.
content: Credit: Andy Baryer / Android Authority My doorbell camera works great at showing who’s at my front door. However, it leaves me with a couple of blind spots. First, it doesn’t show my package at the bottom of the door when it’s delivered. If I’m not home, that package might sit there for hours, making it vulnerable to theft by a porch pirate. My low-tech solution was to put a sign under the door asking the driver to place the package into a box next to my door. However, this creates a second blind spot because my doorbell camera doesn’t show packages going into the box. With the Blurams F20C 4K Solar Outdoor Security Camera, my goal was to eliminate these two blind spots. I mounted it to a tree that faces my front door so I can see if the driver leaves the package at the front door or if they put it into the delivery box. So, is a solar-powered camera with no wires reliable enough to keep watch over my deliveries all day?

Select features also support older models, with improved Sleep Coaching extending back to the Galaxy Watch 4. Samsung could break its tradition of launching a new Galaxy Watch every year as early as 2027, reportedly shifting its focus to software updates and new health features for existing smartwatches. We’re already seeing what that approach could mean for Galaxy Watch owners, as Samsung has confirmed that several health and fitness features from the Galaxy Watch 9 are making their way to last year’s models. title: New Play Store requirements force app developers to publish their addresses online
summary: The only way to avoid Google's requirement is to pull your apps from Europe and the UK.
content: Credit: Megan Ellis / Android Authority TL;DR Google is reportedly facing privacy concerns over a requirement for app developers to disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses. The requirement applies to all app developers, including solo creators, who offer their apps in Europe and the UK. The company won’t allow developers to use a PO box, leading at least one creator to say they might rent a separate office. Google and partners started rolling out developer verification for Android apps earlier this year, along with a more convoluted sideloading process on devices. These new measures will launch globally in January , but another Google requirement is under scrutiny due to privacy issues. The Elec reports that Google is facing privacy concerns over a recent requirement that app developers (including solo creators) publicly disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses on Google Play. This move, which kicks in from March 2027, is meant to help Google and developers comply with European regulatory requirements. However, the outlet adds that developer addresses and phone numbers will be shown worldwide.

title: Google says Gemini’s Chrome RAM-hogging issue is finally resolved
summary: Gemini in Chrome won't use too much of your RAM anymore.
content: TL;DR Google has confirmed that the high memory usage issue in Gemini’s web app has been fixed. Users have been reporting Gemini using massive amounts of RAM in Chrome for over a year. Google hasn’t explained what was wrong or what it fixed. If you use Gemini in Chrome, you may have noticed that it can slow your computer down to a crawl. Users have been complaining about Gemini’s RAM usage on the web for a long time, especially when it’s running in a Chrome tab. Fortunately, that may no longer be a problem. Reddit user That_Discussion_7513 posted a screenshot of Gemini in Chrome using over 5GB of RAM on their PC. In a comment on their post, the official Google Support account said the issue has been resolved. It also asked users to report back if they still see high memory usage in Chrome. The company didn’t explain what was wrong or what it fixed.

On Pixel phones, this is part of Notifications Intelligence, and Google now appears to be working to include a new feature to emphasize high-priority notifications. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. title: Motorola’s Android 17 update breaks cover screen calling features for some Razr users
summary: Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.
content: TL;DR Some Motorola Razr users report losing access to the dial pad and contacts on the cover screen after updating to Android 17. The issue appears to stem from Motorola replacing its native Phone app with Google’s, with no easy way to switch back. Rotating the phone or reducing the display and font sizes has helped some affected users restore the missing functionality. One of the biggest selling points of Motorola’s Razr phones is how much you can do without ever unfolding them. We’ve previously put this versatility to the test , but something as basic as making a phone call from the cover screen is now proving difficult for some Razr owners following the Android 17 update. Affected users say the update replaced Motorola’s native Phone app with Google’s alternative. While the new app works as expected on the main display, the cover screen experience is different. Users report that they can still access recent calls but can no longer open the dial pad or access contacts without opening the phone.

title: Motorola Signature 27 hands-on: A $1,600 flagship that Samsung and Google can’t match
summary: The Motorola Signature 27 is a worthy flagship, but it takes more than top-tier specs to create a winning device.
content: It’s not a secret that the Motorola Signature 27 was near the top of my list of flagship phones I wanted in 2026. Moto’s been teasing us for years about returning to the US market with a traditional, slab flagship device, and it’s finally a reality. Over the last couple of years, the company has set the table with the well-received Razr lineup. Motorola’s foldables are a sales hit and for good reason. Now, Motorola hopes that success will extend to the Signature 27. It carries a hefty price tag, but that just seems to be the new reality for smartphones in 2026 and beyond. However, Moto packs plenty for your $1,600. I’ve spent extensive hands-on time with the Signature 27, and here’s why you’ll want one — and why Motorola needs to finish what it started.

title: OnePlus reveals ColorOS 17 plans for native apps, paid AI features, and more
summary: More native apps are coming, but some AI features will cost you.
content: TL;DR OnePlus is exploring wider availability of its native Phone app and plans to bring OPPO’s Calendar app to its devices. ColorOS 17 users can pay for additional AI usage or wait for their free allowance to reset. OnePlus plans to add AI Photo Agent in a future update but has confirmed the removal of its iconic Calculator Easter egg. The transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS has brought plenty of changes to OnePlus phones. And while many of our readers have warmed up to the new software , not everything has been well received by fans. From missing features to the future of native OnePlus apps, the company has now addressed some of the biggest questions surrounding ColorOS 17, revealing what users can expect from future updates and what’s already gone for good. In a recent AMA on the OnePlus Community forum , OnePlus revealed that it’s exploring plans to bring its native dialer to more markets. Many OnePlus phones ship with Google Phone, while users in markets like India have access to the company’s own calling app, complete with features such as call recording without an audible announcement, AI-powered call summaries, and real-time translations . More users could eventually ditch Google’s dialer, although availability, including call recording support, will depend on the device and region.

title: Pixel users report broken always-on display in Android Auto after November update
summary: Even the newest Pixel phones aren't spared.
content: TL;DR Pixel users report that the November update breaks the always-on display when connected to Android Auto. The issue affects multiple generations, including the Pixel 9, Pixel 10, and Pixel 11 series. We’ve reached out to Google to see whether it’s aware of the bug and working on a fix. Google’s November update for Pixel phones has already caused a fair share of headaches, from broken lock screen shortcuts to issues with the always-on display and notifications . It turns out the update may have introduced yet another display-related bug, this time affecting Pixel owners who use Android Auto. Pixel owners across Reddit and the Android Auto Help community report that their phones’ always-on displays stop working when connected to Android Auto. Instead of showing the time, notifications, and other glanceable information, the screen remains completely black until they disconnect from their cars.

title: Samsung’s Recompose tool could let you shift a photo’s perspective with AI in One UI 9.5
summary: Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals a Photo Assist tool that could convert still shots into 3D scenes to change camera angles.
content: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 suggests Samsung is working on Recompose, a Galaxy AI tool in Photo Assist that could let you change a photo’s angle and perspective after you’ve taken it. Recompose appears to build a 3D version of your photo on-device using Samsung’s Spatial Core add-on, before Samsung’s cloud generates the final image. Recompose is hidden on the Galaxy S26 Ultra for now, and the same code shows Photo Assist’s Style tool switching to a new image model labeled “GPT”. Samsung has been steadily turning its Gallery app into a Galaxy AI photo editor. Photo Assist can already erase objects , move and resize them, expand backgrounds, restyle your shots, and edit them with text prompts. With One UI 9.5, Samsung also added a Live effect tool that turns still photos into 3D wallpapers . Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests the two ideas are coming together. Samsung appears to be working on a tool called Recompose, which could let you change the angle of a photo after you’ve taken it. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. Recompose could let you change the angle of your photos We found Recompose inside Samsung’s Photo Editor app in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra. It sits within Photo Assist’s Move tool, which currently only lets you straighten a photo on the S26 Ultra. On supported devices, the Move tool could gain a switch button to toggle between “Move” and “Recompose”, along with a reset button.

title: Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s
summary: Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals an unreleased "SPAC" framework to process anonymized cloud-based Galaxy AI requests.
content: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to “SPAC,” a new Samsung framework for processing AI requests on its servers while keeping them private. SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6. SPAC doesn’t seem to be active on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung hasn’t announced it either. Galaxy AI has always made you choose between privacy and capability. Features that run on your phone keep your data there. However, the more capable ones, like Writing assist, Note assist, and generative photo edits, send your data to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s current promise for those is a policy one: Photo Editor, for instance, tells you your image “will be sent to servers for processing… but not stored by Samsung.” If you’d rather not take that on trust and face value , the only option is the “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings, which switches those cloud-based features off entirely. Apple pitched a way around that trade-off two years ago when it launched Private Cloud Compute with Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. Private Cloud Compute (PCC) promises to extend device-level privacy to server-side AI processing: your request still goes to a server, but it’s encrypted, anonymized, and processed in a way that even Apple says it can’t access. Google and Meta have since built their own versions, with Google promising your personal data stays private to you and is not accessible to anyone else, “not even Google.” Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests Samsung is building its own take on the idea, and it looks a lot like Apple’s.

title: Samsung is killing Quick Share’s Private sharing, and it’s already gone in One UI 9.5 beta
summary: A Galaxy Store update warns of the upcoming shutdown, while One UI 9.5 Beta 1 removes the toggle and code entirely.
content: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has added an advance notice to the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5 warning that it plans to discontinue the Private sharing feature. Once the shutdown takes effect, users will not be able to send or receive files through Private sharing, and recipients will lose access to previously shared files. Samsung has not announced a specific cutoff date, though the toggle and code are already removed in Quick Share v13.9.50.30 on One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Samsung’s Quick Share has evolved rapidly this year, gaining features like AirDrop compatibility on the Galaxy S26 series and preparing for Tap to Share in One UI 9.5 . However, not every tool is making the cut. Samsung is now officially warning users that it plans to discontinue Quick Share’s Private sharing feature. The warning appears in the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5, which lists an “Advance notice of the upcoming discontinuation of the ‘Private sharing’ feature”.

title: You can now change YouTube’s app icon on your phone, but only if you pay for it
summary: Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.
content: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube is now letting Premium subscribers change its app icon. The current selection includes three options for the icon. YouTube has been testing seven app icons in total, but four are missing from the current rollout. Several prominent apps, including X, Telegram, Reddit, and Instagram, let users swap out the default app icon for something else. Often, this perk is available only to users who pay for the experience. Last month, we learned that YouTube is also working on a similar feature that lets Premium subscribers change the app icon, and it already appears to be rolling out for some folks. User Radu Oncescu on X posted screenshots of the setting that lets users change the default icon to one of the three other options currently available. These include one with a shiny, metal-like finish, somewhat like a silver YouTube Play button, another one featuring what look like brush strokes using red paint, and a third one with a pixel effect and a gradient over the icon.
